diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..737fb4280de112a481fb9d3485ec25251ed00ddb 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -360,6 +360,9 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
     create a nicer looking title. :func:`titleize` is meant for creating pretty
     output.
 
+    Words written in capitals, such as acronyms, are kept as they are if the
+    string also contains lowercase letters.
+
     Examples::
 
       >>> titleize("man from the boondocks")
@@ -370,13 +373,39 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       'The Man Without A Past'
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
 
     """
-    return re.sub(
-        r"\b('?\w)",
-        lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
-        humanize(underscore(word)).title()
-    )
+    if not any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        # There is no telling acronyms from other words in an all-caps string
+        # like "HELLO WORLD", so it is titleized as it always has been.
+        return re.sub(
+            r"\b('?\w)",
+            lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
+            humanize(underscore(word)).title()
+        )
+
+    def capitalize(match: typing.Match[str]) -> str:
+        apostrophe, part = match.groups()
+        # Keep words in capitals, like "NASA" or "DON'T", and plural acronyms,
+        # like "URLs", but not a capital after an apostrophe in a word that
+        # isn't, like "David'S".
+        if (part.isupper() or _is_plural_acronym(part)) and (
+                not apostrophe or match.string[match.start() - 1].isupper()):
+            return match.group()
+        part = part.lower().title()
+        if apostrophe:
+            part = part[0].lower() + part[1:]
+        return apostrophe + part
+
+    # The same as humanize(underscore(word)), except that the case is kept
+    word = _separate_words(word)
+    word = re.sub(r"_[iI][dD]$", "", word)
+    word = word.replace("_", " ")
+    return re.sub(r"\b('?)(\w+)", capitalize, word)
 
 
 def transliterate(string: str) -> str:
@@ -413,10 +442,25 @@ def underscore(word: str) -> str:
         'IoError'
 
     """
-    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    return _separate_words(word).lower()
+
+
+def _separate_words(word: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put underscores between the words of a CamelCase or dashed string, like
+    :func:`underscore` does, but keep the case of the letters.
+
+    An acronym in the plural, like ``"URLs"``, is one word and not split into
+    ``"UR"`` and ``"Ls"``.
+    """
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z](?!s\b)[a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
     word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
-    word = word.replace("-", "_")
-    return word.lower()
+    return word.replace("-", "_")
+
+
+def _is_plural_acronym(word: str) -> bool:
+    """Tell whether ``word`` is an acronym in the plural, like ``"URLs"``."""
+    return len(word) > 2 and word.endswith("s") and word[:-1].isupper()

description: a shared word splitter that keeps plural acronyms like 'URLs' whole (for titleize) is also used by underscore(), changing its output: underscore('URLs') == 'urls' and underscore('REST APIs') == 'rest apis' instead of base 'ur_ls' / 'rest ap_is' (underscore('NASARocket') is still 'nasa_rocket')
